userStories.title: Route commit indexing through the configured CodeExtractor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Select the extraction implementation through API configuration and inject it into indexCommit while preserving all post-extraction indexing behavior.

**Motivation** — The planned production api container limit is 512 MiB.

**Approach** — Extraction mode and indexCommit (US-002).

- Mode is read by `readCodeIntelConfig(env)` from `CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE`: `child` (default when unset or empty) or `inprocess`. Any other value throws. `createCodeExtractor(config, graph)` returns the matching implementation. `CodeIntelModule` provides `CodeExtractor` through a factory that calls `createCodeExtractor(readCodeIntelConfig(process.env), graph)`.
- `apps/api/.env.test` sets `CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE=inprocess`. Tests run the api from TypeScript source, where the built child script does not exist, so suites that index through the real module use the in-process extractor. `apps/api/.env.example` documents the variable.
- `AstIndexService.indexCommit` awaits `CodeExtractor.extract(files)` instead of calling `codeGraph.extractBatch(files)`. Everything after extraction is unchanged. When `extract` rejects, `indexCommit` rejects with the same error before it opens the transaction, so no symbol is deleted or written and the outbox retries the event. On the HTTP index route (`codeintel.index.write`) the rejection is not mapped: it propagates like any other unexpected error from `indexCommit`.

Changed integration: `AstIndexService` constructor baseline `(codeGraph: CodeGraphService, symbolStore: SymbolStore, txManager: ITransactionManager)` becomes `(codeGraph: CodeGraphService, symbolStore: SymbolStore, txManager: ITransactionManager, extractor: CodeExtractor)`. `codeGraph` stays because `resolveRelationships` is still called on it. `AstIndexService.indexCommit` replaces `const extractions = this.codeGraph.extractBatch(files)` with `const extractions = await this.extractor.extract(files)`; signature unchanged. Invalid CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE must throw an Error that names the variable.

Existing-test migration, without changing assertions: `apps/api/src/code-intel/ast-index.service.spec.ts` passes a fourth argument, an extractor whose `extract` resolves with `codeGraph.extractBatch(files)`, so its existing assertions on `extractBatch` and on the index result keep holding. `apps/api/src/code-intel/ast-index.batch.spec.ts` updates its four constructor calls with an extractor whose `extract` resolves with `graph.extractBatch(files)`; its assertions that `graph.extractBatch` is called once with the files stay true through that extractor. `apps/api/src/code-intel/ast-index.project-scope.spec.ts` passes the same kind of fourth argument; the delete-before-upsert order and project-scoped id assertions stay unchanged. `apps/api/test/unit/ast-index.service.unit.spec.ts` adds a `CodeExtractor` provider whose `extract` calls `mockCodeGraph.extractBatch(files)` at call time (the tests reassign that mock's return value per case) and resolves with the result. Its assertions on `extractBatch` stay true through that extractor. The replacing invariant is AC-7.

Seams: US-002 consumes `CodeExtractor`, `InProcessCodeExtractor` and `ChildProcessCodeExtractor` (US-001). US-002 AC-7 stubs `CodeExtractor.extract` and drives `AstIndexService.indexCommit`; US-002 AC-8 enters one level higher, at `CodeCommitOutboxHandler.process`, the handler the `code_commit` outbox event reaches, with a real `AstIndexService` behind it. US-002 AC-6 proves the module provides the extractor that `readCodeIntelConfig` selects: `.env.test` sets `inprocess`, so the test stubs `child` to show the factory reads the environment. Reuse `code-commit-outbox-handler.spec.ts` mocked decryptToken/createVcsProvider, connection and config setup; do not change the production handler. Add co-located config/extractor specs and a database-free module-compilation assertion using GlobalStubsModule, vi.stubEnv and environment restoration.

**Scope** — In: code-intel.config.ts, factory DI provider, AstIndexService's fourth dependency and awaited extraction, .env.test/.env.example, the four existing fixture migrations and the new config/indexing/seam tests. Out: extractor implementations, child protocol, entry script and build probe belong to US-001; SSE, VCS HTTP policy, EntityStore and runner hardening belong to US-003 through US-006. Filtering and capping the commit indexer's input (koda #534 steps 1 and 2): shipped separately; `code-commit-outbox-handler.ts` is not changed here.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// apps/api/src/code-intel/code-intel.config.ts
export type CodeExtractionMode = 'child' | 'inprocess';
export function readCodeIntelConfig(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): { extractionMode: CodeExtractionMode }
export function createCodeExtractor(config: { extractionMode: CodeExtractionMode }, graph: CodeGraphService): CodeExtractor
```
Target AstIndexService constructor: `(codeGraph: CodeGraphService, symbolStore: SymbolStore, txManager: ITransactionManager, extractor: CodeExtractor)`. Preserve TRANSACTION_MANAGER injection and the existing indexCommit signature, result shape, project-scoped symbol IDs, relationship resolution and transaction callback.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] readCodeIntelConfig({}) and readCodeIntelConfig({ CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE: '' }) each return { extractionMode: 'child' }.
AC-2 [unit] readCodeIntelConfig({ CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE: 'inprocess' }) returns { extractionMode: 'inprocess' }.
AC-3 [unit] readCodeIntelConfig({ CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE: 'thread' }) throws an Error whose message contains CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE.
AC-4 [unit] createCodeExtractor({ extractionMode: 'inprocess' }, new CodeGraphService()) returns an instance of InProcessCodeExtractor.
AC-5 [unit] createCodeExtractor({ extractionMode: 'child' }, new CodeGraphService()) returns an instance of ChildProcessCodeExtractor.

AC-6 [unit] With CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE stubbed to child through vi.stubEnv before the module is compiled and restored after the test, a testing module compiled from GlobalStubsModule and CodeIntelModule (as code-intel.module.spec.ts does) returns an instance of ChildProcessCodeExtractor for moduleRef.get(CodeExtractor); constructing it spawns nothing.

AC-7 [unit] With an extractor whose extract resolves with one symbols result per file, indexCommit('acme/widgets', 'c1', [{ path: 'src/a.ts', content: 'A' }, { path: 'src/b.ts', content: 'B' }], 'proj-1') calls extract exactly once with those two files in that order, and never calls codeGraph.extractBatch.

AC-8 [unit] With a CodeCommitOutboxHandler built over a real AstIndexService (a real CodeGraphService, stub symbol store, pass-through transaction manager, stub extractor resolving one symbols result per file) a repository stub returning a VCS connection, a config with encryptionKey set, decryptToken mocked and createVcsProvider mocked to return a provider whose fetchCommitFiles resolves [{ path: 'src/a.ts', content: 'A' }] (the setup code-commit-outbox-handler.spec.ts uses), process({ repoId: 'acme/widgets', commitHash: 'c1', ref: 'refs/heads/main', projectId: 'p1', changedFiles: ['src/a.ts'] }) calls the extractor's extract once with [{ path: 'src/a.ts', content: 'A' }].
AC-9 [unit] When extract rejects with new CodeExtractionError(...) of reason 'timeout', indexCommit rejects with that same error instance.
AC-10 [unit] When extract rejects with a CodeExtractionError, indexCommit never calls symbolStore.deleteByFile or symbolStore.upsertSymbol.
AC-11 [unit] When extract rejects with a CodeExtractionError, indexCommit never calls the transaction manager's run.

routing.reasoning: US-001 supplies the abstraction and process lifecycle; this story adds standard mode parsing, one Nest factory and an awaited delegate within code-intel, plus mechanical constructor-fixture migration, without changing authentication, encryption or transaction internals.

modifiedFiles.reason: it builds `new AstIndexService(codeGraph, symbolStore, txManager)` with three arguments; it passes a fourth, an extractor whose `extract` resolves with `codeGraph.extractBatch(files)`, so its existing assertions on `extractBatch` and on the index result keep holding. The replacing invariant is US-002 AC-7.

its four `new AstIndexService(graph, store, tx)` calls pass a fourth argument, an extractor whose `extract` resolves with `graph.extractBatch(files)`; its assertions that `graph.extractBatch` is called once with the files stay true through that extractor. The replacing invariant is US-002 AC-7.

its `new AstIndexService(graph, store, tx)` call passes a fourth argument, an extractor whose `extract` resolves with `graph.extractBatch(files)`; the delete-before-upsert order and project-scoped id assertions stay unchanged.

it builds `AstIndexService` through `Test.createTestingModule` with a `providers` list that has no `CodeExtractor`, so the module no longer compiles; it adds a `CodeExtractor` provider whose `extract` calls `mockCodeGraph.extractBatch(files)` at call time (the tests reassign that mock's return value per case) and resolves with the result. Its assertions on `extractBatch` stay true through that extractor.

userStories.title: Close SSE streams after two stalled-client heartbeat readings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Detect sustained socket backlog in all four SSE routes and complete the stream before its unread event queue grows indefinitely.

**Motivation** — `createLiveStream` pushes every event and heartbeat; Nest writes them one at a time and waits for the socket to drain, so events for a client that no longer reads queue in memory until the TCP connection times out.

**Approach** — Stalled live stream (US-003).

- `LiveStreamOptions` gains an optional `isStalled: () => boolean`. On each heartbeat tick that passes the existing `done` and `checking` guard, `createLiveStream` reads it first; a tick that guard skips is not counted. When it returns true on two consecutive ticks, the stream completes on the second tick without checking access and without sending a ping. A false reading resets the count. Without `isStalled` the stream behaves as today.
- `socketHasBacklog(req)` returns a function that reports whether the request's socket has unsent bytes: `req.raw.socket.writableLength > 0` for a Fastify request, `req.socket.writableLength > 0` for a plain Node request, and false when neither socket is present. It reads the socket on every call.
- A socket has unsent bytes only while the kernel send buffer is full, so two readings one heartbeat apart (25 s by default) mean the client is not reading. A browser `EventSource` reconnects by itself.
- The four SSE routes pass `isStalled: socketHasBacklog(req)`.

The four routes are LiveController.events in apps/api/src/live/live.controller.ts, MeLiveController.events in apps/api/src/live/me-live.controller.ts, ThreadEventsController.events in apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-events.controller.ts and WorkspaceThreadEventsController.events in apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-thread-events.controller.ts. Preserve their guards, JWT extraction, permissions, membership checks and shared stream-slot lifecycle. Existing done/checking guards, timer clamps, access failure behavior, ready/event emission, expiry and once-only teardown remain intact.

Seams: US-003 wires `socketHasBacklog` into four existing routes. AC-10 to AC-13 call each controller's `@Sse()` method, the method Nest invokes for the route, and observe the returned stream. AC-10 and AC-11 reuse the request the existing controller specs build (a Bearer JWT header) and add `raw.socket`. AC-12 and AC-13 pre-set `req.threadEvents` and `req.workspaceThreadEvents`, which the route guards set in production, and cast the request to add `raw.socket`. The SSE controller specs (`live.controller.spec.ts` and its three siblings) already build each controller and call `events(...)`. Keep existing tests unchanged; implement additional stream/controller assertions in the new co-located stalled spec using equivalent fixtures. Use Vitest fake timers with async advancement and restore timers after each test.

**Scope** — In: optional stream backlog callback, consecutive-reading lifecycle, socket-backlog helper, four route option additions and new helper/stalled-stream tests. Out: extraction/config activation, VCS transport, ticket entities and runner changes belong to the other stories; do not redesign SSE authorization or buffering. US-003 only: a test of a heartbeat tick that the `checking` guard skips; the rule is stated in Design and the counted ticks are tested. US-003 only: confirming under Bun in a deployed container that a stalled client's socket reports unsent bytes; that is a manual live check after deploy.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// apps/api/src/live/socket-backlog.ts
export function socketHasBacklog(req: unknown): () => boolean

// apps/api/src/live/live-stream.ts
export function createLiveStream<E extends LiveStreamEvent = LiveEvent>(options: LiveStreamOptions<E>): Observable<MessageEvent>
```
`LiveStreamOptions` baseline: `{ key, heartbeatMs, expiresAtMs, now, subscribe, stillAllowed, onClose }`. Target: the same fields plus optional `isStalled?: () => boolean`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] Given expiresAtMs null and stillAllowed resolving true, a stream from createLiveStream with isStalled always returning true completes on its second heartbeat tick, and onClose is called once.

AC-2 [unit] Given expiresAtMs null and stillAllowed resolving true, for a stream from createLiveStream with isStalled always returning true, stillAllowed is called on the first heartbeat tick and not on the second.
AC-3 [unit] Given expiresAtMs null and stillAllowed resolving true, for a stream from createLiveStream with isStalled always returning true, no ping event is emitted on the second heartbeat tick.
AC-4 [unit] With isStalled returning true, false, true on three consecutive ticks and stillAllowed resolving true, the stream is not completed after the third tick.
AC-5 [unit] With no isStalled option and stillAllowed resolving true, three heartbeat ticks emit three ping events and the stream is not completed.
AC-6 [unit] socketHasBacklog({ raw: { socket: { writableLength: 10 } } })() returns true.
AC-7 [unit] socketHasBacklog({ socket: { writableLength: 10 } })() returns true.

AC-8 [unit] For a request object whose raw.socket.writableLength is 0, the function socketHasBacklog returned gives false, and gives true after that writableLength is set to 5 without calling socketHasBacklog again.
AC-9 [unit] socketHasBacklog({})() returns false.
AC-10 [unit] The stream LiveController.events returns for a request whose raw.socket.writableLength stays 5 completes after two heartbeat intervals.
AC-11 [unit] The stream MeLiveController.events returns for a request whose raw.socket.writableLength stays 5 completes after two heartbeat intervals.
AC-12 [unit] The stream ThreadEventsController's @Sse() method returns for a request whose raw.socket.writableLength stays 5 completes after two heartbeat intervals.
AC-13 [unit] The stream WorkspaceThreadEventsController's @Sse() method returns for a request whose raw.socket.writableLength stays 5 completes after two heartbeat intervals.

routing.reasoning: The implementation is a two-reading counter, a socket reader and repeated option wiring across four existing controllers, not a new streaming architecture; strict security TDD remains required because heartbeat ordering controls existing access revalidation and authenticated stream teardown.

userStories.title: Bound VCS HTTP requests and refuse redirects
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give the VCS default native-fetch client a configurable timeout and prevent redirects from forwarding provider credentials.

**Motivation** — The GitLab provider authenticates with a `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header, which `fetch` keeps when it follows a redirect to another origin.

**Approach** — VCS HTTP client (US-004).

- `createDefaultHttpClient(options?)` is exported from `vcs/factory.ts` and takes `{ timeoutMs?: number }`, default `VCS_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` (30,000).
- `get` and `post` pass `redirect: 'manual'` and `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` to `fetch`.
- A 3xx response is not followed. It takes the existing not-ok path, so the call rejects with the error `httpError` builds, whose `response.status` is the 3xx status.

Failure handling: A VCS `fetch` does not answer within `timeoutMs`: the call rejects. A VCS endpoint answers 3xx: the call rejects with an error whose `response.status` is that status. Preserve existing GET params and returned headers, POST JSON encoding and headers, response bodies, non-OK error shape and explicitly injected HttpClient behavior. Mirror FleetHttpClient's timeout/redirect policy, not its error mapping or dependency wiring.

Seam: `createVcsProvider` already calls `createDefaultHttpClient()` when no `httpClient` is supplied; AC-6 enters at `createVcsProvider`. Add default-http-client.spec.ts with restored global fetch stubs: return a real 200 JSON Response for options assertions, a 302 for httpError, and a pending promise that rejects on its provided signal for both timeout assertions. Existing factory.spec.ts is not modified.

**Scope** — In: export and extend the default client in apps/api/src/vcs/factory.ts, define its 30,000 ms default, apply policy to GET and POST and add native-client/factory-seam tests. Out: extraction, SSE, EntityStore and runner work belongs to the other stories. Routing the VCS providers through `FleetHttpClient`, and capping the size of a VCS response body. Following a same-origin redirect in the VCS client: a renamed repository that answers 301 now fails until its connection URL is updated.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// apps/api/src/vcs/factory.ts
export function createDefaultHttpClient(options?: { timeoutMs?: number }): HttpClient
```
Baseline is module-private `function createDefaultHttpClient(): HttpClient`; createVcsProvider and the existing HttpClient get/post signatures and response shapes are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] With the global fetch stubbed to resolve a 200 JSON response, createDefaultHttpClient().get('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {} }) calls fetch with redirect equal to 'manual' and a signal that is an AbortSignal.

AC-2 [unit] With the global fetch stubbed to resolve a 200 JSON response, createDefaultHttpClient().post('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {}, body: {} }) calls fetch with redirect equal to 'manual' and a signal that is an AbortSignal.
AC-3 [unit] With fetch stubbed to resolve a response of status 302, createDefaultHttpClient().get('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {} }) rejects with an error whose response.status is 302.

AC-4 [unit] With fetch stubbed to stay pending until its signal aborts and then reject, createDefaultHttpClient({ timeoutMs: 50 }).get('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {} }) rejects within one second.

AC-5 [unit] With fetch stubbed to stay pending until its signal aborts and then reject, createDefaultHttpClient({ timeoutMs: 50 }).post('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {}, body: {} }) rejects within one second.

AC-6 [unit] With fetch stubbed to resolve a 200 JSON response whose body is { default_branch: 'main' }, createVcsProvider('github', { provider: 'github', token: 't', repoUrl: 'https://github.com/acme/widgets' }).getDefaultBranch() calls fetch with redirect equal to 'manual'.

routing.reasoning: Only factory.ts changes at runtime: export the existing function, add an optional timeout and two standard fetch options while retaining httpError; strict security TDD is mandatory because redirect handling protects provider tokens.

suggestedCriteria: Given a 200 JSON response with body { value: 1 } and header x-test: ok, createDefaultHttpClient().get('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: {} }) resolves with data { value: 1 } and headers containing x-test: ok, preserving the existing response shape.

Given a 200 JSON response, createDefaultHttpClient().post('https://api.example.test/x', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer t' }, body: { value: 1 } }) sends the JSON serialization of { value: 1 } with the supplied Authorization header and Content-Type application/json, preserving the existing POST contract.

userStories.title: Remove deleted tickets from the retrieval EntityStore
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove the project-scoped ticket entity on TICKET_DELETED without rereading or recreating the deleted ticket.

**Motivation** — A `TICKET_DELETED` event re-reads the ticket instead of removing its entity.

**Approach** — EntityStore (US-005).

- `EntityStore.removeEntity(projectId, id)` deletes one ticket entity of that project and does nothing when it is absent. Entities of other projects and `code_module` entities are not touched.
- `handleOutboxEvent` for a `ticket_event` whose payload `action` is `'TICKET_DELETED'` and that carries a string `ticketId` and `projectId` calls `removeEntity(projectId, ticketId)` and returns, without reading the ticket. This check comes before the existing `payload.ticket` branch.

Failure handling: `TICKET_DELETED` for a ticket the store does not hold: `handleOutboxEvent` resolves, nothing changes. Keep the ordinary ticket-event reindex path, including TICKET_UPDATED, unchanged. Do not confuse this retrieval store with src/entity-graph's stores.

Seam: `EntityStoreWarmup.onModuleInit` already registers the `ticket_event` handler on `FanOutPublisher` and forwards to `EntityStore.handleOutboxEvent`; AC-7 enters at the registered handler. Construct EntityStoreWarmup over a real store and a registry stub that records callbacks, then invoke the callback with a deletion payload; do not call a database or change registration. Existing entity-store.spec.ts assertions remain unchanged; add entity-store.ticket-deleted.spec.ts for removal, project isolation, absence/idempotency, no-read, update and fan-out seam behavior.

**Scope** — In: removeEntity, the deletion-first ticket_event branch and co-located behavioral tests through both the store and existing warmup registry. Out: extraction, SSE, VCS and runner changes belong to the other stories; no redesign of graph refresh, ranking or warmup. Removing a deleted project's entities from `EntityStore`: `clear(projectId)` already exists and its callers are unchanged. US-005 only: an entity of another source (for example a `code_module`) that shares a ticket's id; `removeEntity` removes ticket entities only.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// apps/api/src/rag/entity-store.ts
removeEntity(projectId: string, id: string): void

// Existing integration, unchanged signatures
indexEntity(projectId: string, entity: Entity): void
searchEntities(projectId: string, query: string): ScoredEntity[]
handleOutboxEvent(event: { eventType: string; payload: unknown }): Promise<void>
```
A ticket_event payload carries `{ id, type: 'ticket_event', action, timestamp, ticketId, projectId, actorId, actorType, data }`; deletion is selected from action and string ids, before any embedded ticket or repository lookup.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] After indexEntity('p1', { id: 't1', label: 'Login bug', tags: ['login', 'bug'], source: 'ticket', sourceId: 't1' }), removeEntity('p1', 't1') makes searchEntities('p1', 'login') return an empty array.
AC-2 [unit] removeEntity('p1', 'missing') on an empty store returns without throwing.
AC-3 [unit] With ticket t1 indexed for both p1 and p2, removeEntity('p1', 't1') leaves getAllEntities('p2') holding the entity with id t1.

AC-4 [unit] With entities t1 and t2 indexed for p1, handleOutboxEvent({ eventType: 'ticket_event', payload: { action: 'TICKET_DELETED', ticketId: 't1', projectId: 'p1' } }) leaves getAllEntities('p1') holding only the entity with id t2.

AC-5 [unit] With a rag repository stub supplied to the store and t1 indexed for p1, handleOutboxEvent for a ticket_event with action 'TICKET_DELETED', ticketId 't1' and projectId 'p1' never calls findTicketById.

AC-6 [unit] handleOutboxEvent for a ticket_event with action 'TICKET_UPDATED', ticketId 't3' and projectId 'p1', with findTicketById resolving { id: 't3', title: 'Export report' }, makes searchEntities('p1', 'export') return the entity with id t3.

AC-7 [unit] With an EntityStoreWarmup built over a real EntityStore holding ticket t1 for p1 and a FanOutPublisher stub that records registered handlers, after onModuleInit() calling the handler registered for ticket_event with { action: 'TICKET_DELETED', ticketId: 't1', projectId: 'p1' } makes searchEntities('p1', 'login') return an empty array for a ticket labelled Login bug.

AC-8 [unit] With only t2 indexed for p1, handleOutboxEvent for a ticket_event with action 'TICKET_DELETED', ticketId 'unknown' and projectId 'p1' resolves and getAllEntities('p1') still holds exactly the entity with id t2.

routing.reasoning: One production-file additive map deletion and event branch, with existing fan-out registration reused unchanged and straightforward database-free assertions.

suggestedCriteria: When a well-formed TICKET_DELETED payload also carries payload.ticket for the deleted ticket, handleOutboxEvent leaves that ticket absent from the project's entities.

userStories.title: Bound runner output scanning and credential request dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stream runner verdict output with bounded per-line memory and dispatch only the first credential request line on each connection.

**Motivation** — `readFixResult`, `reviewPosted` and `HostExecutor.readFixOutcome` load a complete nax output file to find one line.

**Approach** — Runner (US-006).

- `scanLines(path, onLine)` in `src/verdict/scan-lines.ts` reads a file as a stream and calls `onLine` once per line, without the line terminator (`\n` or `\r\n`). It resolves `false` when the file does not exist and `true` otherwise. `onLine` may return `'stop'` to end the scan. A line longer than `MAX_SCAN_LINE_BYTES` (65,536) is delivered once, cut to its first `MAX_SCAN_LINE_BYTES` bytes; the rest of that line is skipped and the next line is delivered normally.
- `readFixResult`, `reviewPosted` and the `fix.stderr` read in `HostExecutor.readFixOutcome` use `scanLines`. Their results are unchanged: `readFixResult` still keeps the first log marker and the last matching result line, and the existing `fix-result.spec.ts`, `fix-result.fix-ready.spec.ts` and `review-posted.spec.ts` pass without edits. The `fix.stderr` scan stops at the first non-blank line.
- `serveRequest` in `credentials/cred-server.ts` reads one request line per connection. Once a newline has arrived it calls `request` once with the text before that newline, trimmed, and ignores every later chunk.

Failure handling: `scanLines` on a missing file resolves `false`, `onLine` never called. `scanLines` on a path that cannot be opened or read for another reason (for example a directory) rejects with that error, as the three callers' reads do today. Empty files resolve true without callbacks. Bound bytes retained for a partial line and skip any overflow until its terminator; do not use a line reader that accumulates an unlimited logical line. Release stream resources on completion, early stop and errors.

Preserve first nonblank stderr selection, diagnostic sanitization/redaction and the 200-character final stderrLine cap; if that selected line sanitizes to null, do not select a later line. Preserve HostExecutor's existing realpath/PR directory fences and readFixState behavior. Only the three specified output scans change, not other HostExecutor reads or generic git output buffering. Fence request receipt before starting its asynchronous reply, separately from the existing answered fence, so extra chunks neither dispatch another request nor grow buffered while a reply is pending. acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] scanLines on a path that does not exist resolves false and never calls onLine.
AC-2 [unit] scanLines on a file holding a, a line feed, b, a carriage return and line feed, then c calls onLine with 'a', 'b', 'c' in that order and resolves true.
AC-3 [unit] When onLine returns 'stop' for the first line of a three-line file, onLine is called exactly once.
AC-4 [unit] For a file whose first line is 200,000 x characters and whose second line is tail, scanLines calls onLine twice: first with a string of MAX_SCAN_LINE_BYTES x characters, then with 'tail'.

AC-8 [unit] Regression guard for existing behaviour: HostExecutor.readFixOutcome for a job whose fix.stderr holds two blank lines, the line fatal: push rejected, then 20,000 further lines returns stderrLine 'fatal: push rejected'.

AC-9 [unit] With serveRequest on a fake socket and a request function returning a promise that stays pending, sending the chunk get plus a line feed and then the same chunk again calls request exactly once.

AC-10 [unit] With serveRequest on a fake socket and a request function returning a promise that stays pending, after the chunk get plus a line feed and then ten further chunks of 1,024 bytes each that each contain a line feed, request has still been called exactly once; after the pending promise resolves, the socket's end is called exactly once, with the JSON of the resolved value followed by a line feed.
AC-11 [unit] Regression guard for existing behaviour: sending the single chunk get, a line feed, then extra calls request once with the line 'get'.
AC-12 [unit] Regression guard for existing behaviour: sending 65 bytes with no line feed answers the socket with the badRequest reply and never calls request.
AC-13 [unit] scanLines on a path that is a directory rejects with an error.
AC-14 [unit] scanLines on an empty file resolves true and never calls onLine.

analysis:
This is an enhancement and hardening bundle over existing API and runner code, not greenfield work. It completes #534 step 3 after the already-shipped input limits (#536), closes #534, and relates to but does not close #535. Preserve exactly US-001 through US-006, with US-002 depending on US-001 and the other stories independently implementable. No CLI, web, database schema, Prisma migration, wire API DTO, or generated client changes are required. The repository guidance identifies the web app as Nuxt rather than the detected Next.js label; neither is relevant to this package-local bundle. The codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct reads and targeted text searches under the supplied execution root. No runtime verification was performed while drafting this PRD.

Architecture and conventions: API code is NestJS/Fastify, CommonJS output running under Bun in production, with TypeScript strict, Vitest/vi.*, SWC decorator metadata, oxlint and Nathapp transaction/DI patterns. Runner code is Bun-only ESM with bun:test. Read .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md and .nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md before implementation; do not edit generated AGENTS.md files. Before writing NestJS code consult the Nathapp capability catalog and package documentation when those tools are available; no new platform abstraction is needed here. Unit and module wiring tests must be database-free; use GlobalStubsModule for module compilation. Avoid adding integration suites for constructor wiring. New API tests belong beside source as *.spec.ts. Runner tests should use real temporary files and the existing injected fixtures rather than live services. Preserve generated acceptance material rather than editing it.

US-001 findings: apps/api/src/code-intel/code-graph.service.ts:26 defines the FileExtraction union; :32-37 retains a lazy ts-morph Project constructor through require, :50-70 extracts a batch synchronously using one project and removes each source file, and :163 resolves relationships without parsing. Consequently the parent can keep CodeGraphService for relationship resolution without loading the compiler if extraction runs solely in a child. The approximately 100 MiB post-GC compiler retention and event-loop blocking motivate a fresh child per extraction; the stated memory measurements are evidence, not test thresholds. apps/api/scripts/check-compiler-load.cjs:1-50 demonstrates an isolated fresh-process check of built CommonJS modules, compiler lazy loading and actual symbol extraction. apps/api/package.json:7 currently builds with nest build, check-dist-requires.ts and check-compiler-load.cjs; append check-extraction-child.cjs after the existing compiler check, preserving both checks. The new child entry must compile to dist/code-intel/extraction-child.js, import reflect-metadata first, keep stdout exclusively JSON, and exit after processing stdin. Default command uses process.execPath, which is Bun in the production build and may differ in tests. Construct ChildProcessCodeExtractor through a factory rather than Nest attempting to inject its primitive constructor parameters. Use a per-instance FIFO that continues after rejection, handles spawn and stdin error events, distinguishes EPIPE from invalid protocol, kills timed-out children with SIGKILL and settles once across competing events. Clear timers and release queue state on every outcome. Do not add worker pools, stdout caps or OS resource limits. Pure protocol/in-process tests run anywhere; real-process extractor tests write temporary .cjs fixture scripts, never invoke the real entry script, and use describe.skipIf(isNaxSandboxed()) with apps/api/test/helpers/test-environment.ts. The declared host testScoped run must verify those process tests; a sandbox skip is not verification. Run bun run --cwd apps/api build to exercise the built entry success path rather than creating a source-mode child dependency.

US-002 findings and impacts: apps/api/src/code-intel/ast-index.service.ts:43-47 has a three-argument constructor and :65 calls codeGraph.extractBatch(files) before any transaction. Relationship resolution at :85-86, delete-before-upsert persistence at :88-125, and onIndexed inside that transaction at :127-129 must remain unchanged after replacing the extraction call with awaited CodeExtractor.extract. Distinguish a rejected extraction request from FileExtraction entries carrying per-file parse errors: request rejection leaves this indexCommit invocation's transaction unopened, while an ordinary per-file parse error still replaces that file's old symbols. Preserve the exact error instance; do not catch/map extraction errors on the HTTP route. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-intel-route.commands.ts:23-39 routes codeintel.index.write directly to indexCommit with its audit callback. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-intel-outbox.subscriber.ts:22-25 registers code_commit, :53-56 delegates to the handler and :78 has a fallback indexCommit call; both receive the new behavior through DI without changing their contracts. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-commit-outbox-handler.ts:55-63 filters input paths, :68 reads a VCS connection, :80-90 obtains a provider via providerForConnection and decryptToken, :103-111 removes oversized files then indexes bounded batches. These input limits and this production handler stay unchanged. Earlier batches or removed-file transactions are not newly rolled back if a later indexCommit fails; the no-write failure invariant applies to the failed invocation, not a new whole-outbox transaction. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-commit-outbox-handler.spec.ts:9-20 already mocks decryptToken and createVcsProvider, with provider/repository/config fixtures at :22-62; reuse that pattern for the real-AstIndexService seam rather than bypassing the handler. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-intel.module.ts:21-36 provides AstIndexService and CodeGraphService but no extractor; add a CodeExtractor useFactory provider reading process.env at module construction. apps/api/src/code-intel/code-intel.module.spec.ts:23-26 compiles GlobalStubsModule plus CodeIntelModule without a DB, the model for the child-mode wiring assertion. Config tests must restore vi.stubEnv. Source-based suites need CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE=inprocess in apps/api/.env.test, which currently has no such setting (apps/api/.env.test:1-12). Document child default and inprocess fallback in .env.example; invalid nonempty modes must name CODE_INTEL_EXTRACTION_MODE in their error. Constructor migration is source-local: apps/api/src/code-intel/ast-index.service.spec.ts:53, ast-index.batch.spec.ts:24/:47/:70/:90 and ast-index.project-scope.spec.ts:27 construct the service directly; pass a fourth extractor that resolves graph.extractBatch(files), retaining existing assertions. apps/api/test/unit/ast-index.service.unit.spec.ts:35-42 supplies Nest providers but no CodeExtractor; add a provider that invokes the mutable mockCodeGraph.extractBatch at call time, not a captured initial return value. Existing controller, outbox, project-scope, batch and e2e coverage should retain their outcomes. US-001 does not itself activate the child; US-002 is the production switch.

US-003 findings and risks: apps/api/src/live/live-stream.ts:13-22 defines LiveStreamOptions and :32-74 builds the Observable. ready and subscription forwarding are :41-44; :48-60 guards done/checking before each asynchronous access check; :69-74 performs timer clearing, bus unsubscribe and onClose. Add the stall counter only for ticks passing that guard, check it before stillAllowed, reset on false and complete on the second consecutive true reading without a second access check or ping. Preserve ready, expiry clamps, revocation handling, event forwarding and exactly-once teardown. socketHasBacklog must read the current request socket on each invocation, supporting Fastify raw.socket and plain Node socket, without caching writableLength or assuming sockets exist in injected tests. The four discovered createLiveStream callers are apps/api/src/live/live.controller.ts:50-58, apps/api/src/live/me-live.controller.ts:42-50, apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-events.controller.ts:96-115 and apps/api/src/fleet/threads/workspace-thread-events.controller.ts:88-98. To respect the spec's no-existing-test-changes rule, new stalled-stream tests may instantiate these controllers using equivalent fixtures in the new spec rather than editing existing specs. Use fake timers plus async advancement to let stillAllowed settle between counted ticks, restore timers, and avoid real sockets. Browser EventSource reconnect is existing behavior, not a client change. US-004 findings and security: apps/api/src/vcs/factory.ts:32-37 implements httpError preserving response.status and parsed body; :42-81 defines a private default HTTP client with GET query handling, JSON POST, response headers and no fetch timeout/redirect policy; :134-137 selects that client only when config.httpClient is absent. Export and extend this existing function without changing HttpClient return shapes, custom client injection, provider selection, headers, params or body serialization. apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/fleet-http-client.ts:23-30 already uses redirect: 'manual' and AbortSignal.timeout, but its RepoCheckException mapping is not the VCS error contract and must not be copied. apps/api/src/vcs/providers/gitlab.provider.ts:103 sends PRIVATE-TOKEN, so stopping cross-origin redirect following is credential hardening, not merely a performance tweak. A 3xx must take the current !response.ok/httpError path; do not follow even same-origin redirects. getDefaultBranch is implemented in the GitHub provider at apps/api/src/vcs/providers/github.provider.ts:179, allowing a createVcsProvider end-to-end factory seam with stubbed global fetch. apps/api/src/vcs/factory.spec.ts:7 onward covers provider construction; leave its assertions unchanged and add default-http-client.spec.ts for native client behavior. US-006 findings and regression anchors: apps/runner/src/verdict/fix-result.ts:32-55 currently readFiles and splits all fix stdout while retaining the first nonempty log marker and last matching result for the assigned PR. readFixState at :59-86 is a separate bounded-purpose JSON/symlink-sensitive path and stays unchanged. apps/runner/src/verdict/review-posted.ts:6-15 similarly reads all stdout then tests a line-start artifact marker. apps/runner/src/executor/host-executor.ts:369-378 delegates to both readers; :381-401 validates PR-directory realpaths and protects state reads, which must not be weakened. :403-413 reads all fix.stderr, chooses its first trimmed nonblank line, sanitizes/redacts it and caps to 200 characters. Replace only those three output scans with scanLines, keeping trusted path checks, redaction, control-only-first-line behavior and return shapes intact. The stderr callback must stop at the first nonblank raw/trimmed line even if sanitization makes it null; do not continue to a later diagnostic. scanLines needs bounded byte accumulation and discard-until-newline state for overlong lines; a generic line reader that buffers an unlimited line is not sufficient. Handle CRLF and the final unterminated line; ENOENT alone resolves false, empty readable files resolve true, and other open/read errors including directories reject. Clean up the file stream on early stop and error. No memory or timing benchmarks are acceptance thresholds. apps/runner/src/credentials/cred-server.ts:46-70 sets answered only when a promise replies, so each data chunk arriving while that promise is pending appends to buffered and calls request again. Add a distinct request-received/processing fence as soon as the first newline arrives, before invoking request, and ignore subsequent chunks; keep answer's exactly-once fence and error/badRequest JSON semantics. Existing verdict tests apps/runner/src/verdict/fix-result.spec.ts:15-43, fix-result.fix-ready.spec.ts and review-posted.spec.ts:10-28 are regression anchors and must pass without edits. apps/runner/test/unit/host-executor.spec.ts:43-59 defines world(), :235-240 defines fixWorld(), and :271-314 verifies diagnostic capping, URL credential redaction, ANSI/control stripping and missing output.
